title: Degradation communications toolkit - templates & playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, customer-facing communications toolkit for service degradations and incidents affecting inference or API responsiveness. It contains ready-to-send status page snippets, short-form customer summaries for outreach, and a customer-friendly postmortem template with remediation and compensation language.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Pick the status update template that matches current impact (brief / intermediate / sustained).
- Fill placeholders ({{INCIDENT_ID}}, {{AFFECTED_FEATURES}}, {{ETA}} etc.).
- Have on-call or SRE review the technical details; CS lead reviews the customer language.
- Post to status.redwood.ai and send targeted customer emails for customers above threshold (see escalation matrix).

Escalation matrix (notes to help pick recipients):
- P0 (complete outage for >5% of requests OR any enterprise SLA-impacting event): All enterprise customers + status page + account teams + exec comms.
- P1 (severe degradation >15m but partial): Affected customers with dedicated notices + status page + account teams.
- P2 (minor increase in latency or error rate): Status page + select customers if they have tight SLOs.

STATUS PAGE UPDATE TEMPLATES
(Each update should be short, time-stamped, and show progress; use plain language; avoid blame.)

1) Short/Initial (use within first 15 minutes)
- Summary: We are currently investigating reports of increased latency and intermittent errors for the Redwood Inference API in region {{REGION}}.
- Impact: Some requests may be slower than expected or return errors (affects text generation and embeddings).
- Mitigation: Engineers are investigating; retrying requests is a temporary workaround.
- Next update: We will provide another update by {{NEXT_UPDATE_TIME}} or sooner.
- Time: {{TIMESTAMP}}

Example: 
- Summary: We are investigating elevated latency for Redwood API requests in us-west-2.
- Impact: Approximately 10% of requests are experiencing delays above 1.5s; a small subset may return 5xx errors.
- Mitigation: Retry logic may help; teams are routing traffic to a healthy pool where possible.
- Next update: +30 minutes or sooner.
- Time: 2026-11-20T15:12Z

2) Intermediate (clearer scope, after 30–90m)
- Summary: We identified a service degradation impacting inference throughput for models >8k context in us-west-2.
- Impact: Customers running long-context generation may see higher latency and rate of errors; ~8–12% of requests affected.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): Autoscaler misconfiguration caused pooling mismatch under a specific traffic mix. Investigation ongoing.
- Workaround: Temporarily routing calls to a compatible model variant (shorter context) reduces failures for most workloads.
- ETA for fix: Targeting a rollback/config bump within 2 hours.
- Next update: We will update at {{NEXT_UPDATE_TIME}} or on completion.
- Time: {{TIMESTAMP}}

3) Sustained / Recovery update (when resolved or mitigated)
- Summary: Service has been restored for the immediate issue affecting inference throughput in us-west-2.
- Impact: Errors and latency have returned to expected levels. Some customers may require session restarts for long-running jobs.
- Resolution: A configuration change to the autoscaler was applied; traffic has been migrated back to primary pools.
- Follow-up: Full post-incident review is underway; we will publish a customer-facing postmortem within 72 hours.
- Time: {{TIMESTAMP}}

CUSTOMER EMAIL BRIEF (concise, targeted outreach for affected enterprise accounts)
Subject: Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — brief impact summary and next steps
Hi {{CUSTOMER_CONTACT_NAME}},
We wanted to make you aware of an incident that affected Redwood Inference in {{REGION}} on {{DATE}}. Short summary: Some inference requests experienced elevated latency and intermittent errors between {{START_TIME}} and {{END_TIME}}.
What we did: Engineers routed traffic to healthy pools and applied a config change to the autoscaler; full recovery achieved at {{RECOVERY_TIME}}.
Impact to you: Based on our logs, your account saw ~{{PCT_AFFECTED}} of requests affected. If you observed any user-facing issues, please tell us and we will prioritize case handling.
Next steps: We’ll share a full, customer-facing postmortem in 72 hours with root cause, remediation, and preventive actions. If you’d like a walkthrough with your account team, we can schedule a 30-minute review.
Apologies for the disruption — we know reliability matters.
Thanks,
{{CS_LEAD_NAME}} (Customer Success) & Redwood Ops

CUSTOMER-FACING POSTMORTEM TEMPLATE
(Designed to be readable by non-technical stakeholders; keep it <2 pages ideally)
Title: Customer post-incident summary — {{INCIDENT_ID}} ({{DATE}}) - Executive summary:
- What happened (one paragraph): Clear, non-blame language describing the service impact and affected capabilities.
- Impact (one paragraph): Which customers/regions/features were affected and the measurable impact (e.g., % of requests, duration).
- Root cause (concise): The technical cause stated plainly with timeline context.
- Mitigation and timeline: What actions restored service and when.
- Customer impact details: If applicable, per-customer brief numbers or guidance for investigating potential data loss or job failures.
- Remediation and prevention: Specific engineering changes, QA/process updates, and monitoring improvements.
- Compensation/credits (if applicable): High-level statement about eligibility for service credits or credits applied, with steps to request.
- Contact and follow-up: How customers can get more details and schedule a debrief.

Example Postmortem (customer version):
- What happened: On 2026-11-20 between 15:05–16:45 UTC, Redwood experienced elevated latency and intermittent 5xx errors for inference requests in us-west-2.
- Impact: ~9% of requests to models with >8k context failed or were delayed; customers running streaming chat or long-context batch jobs were most impacted.
- Root cause: An autoscaler configuration change introduced a race across new pooling logic causing a subset of nodes to drain incorrectly under bursty traffic.
- Mitigation: The change was rolled back at 16:12 UTC and traffic routed to healthy nodes; normal behavior resumed by 16:45 UTC.
- Remediation: We will add a staged rollout gate to autoscaler changes, increase test coverage for the pooling behavior, and add a synthetic long-context traffic test to our CI. ETA for actions: 30 days for rollout gating; 14 days for synthetic test.
- Credits: Affected customers will be eligible for a credit proportional to estimated impacted tokens; contact your account team to start the credit request process.
- Contact: cs-ops@redwood.ai for immediate questions; your Account Executive for prioritization.

Communication cadence & approvals (internal)
- Initial status page: CS lead + on-call engineer approve (aim within 15 mins).
- Customer emails to enterprise: CS lead + SRE manager sign-off.
- Customer-facing postmortem: Draft by SRE, reviewed by CS + Legal for credit language, final sign-off by Head of CS.

Internal checklist before sending customer postmortem:
- Confirm timeline entries with SRE runbook logs and tracing (trace ids noted).
- Verify impacted customer list from billing/usage logs.
- Draft credit estimation model and have finance review if material.
- Redaction check for internal-only debug details.
- Legal review if incident touches compliance/data retention.

Message style guide (customer-facing):
- Use plain language; avoid internal acronyms.
- Be explicit about impact and remediation; don’t overpromise.
- Offer next steps and a contact for follow-up.
- Keep tone apologetic and accountable.

Sample short FAQ for customers (append to postmortem)
Q: Will my data/jobs be lost?
A: No evidence of data loss; some in-flight jobs failed and should be retried. If you need assistance replaying or diagnosing failures, contact cs-ops@redwood.ai.
Q: When will this be prevented in the future?
A: We list planned mitigations above with estimated timelines. We will report back when each milestone is complete.

Working notes / internal fragments (useful copy/paste bits):
- "We are deploying a rollback to autoscaler config to restore healthy pool sizes."
- "Temporary mitigation: route long-context calls to model-x-compat that does not rely on the new pooling path."
- "Postmortem ETA: publish customer version within 72 hours, technical RCA within 7 days."

Appendix: Example token-based credit calculation (for CS/finance use)
- Steps: 1) Estimate number of failed tokens = sum(failed_requests * avg_tokens). 2) Convert to credit = failed_tokens * per_token_rate * credit_factor. 3) Review with finance and Legal.

Notes to self:
- Keep templates short; status page needs 1–3 bullets, not a novel.
- Always include a clear next update time.
- Centralize final postmortems under Confluence and link from status page.

End of doc.
